title: Steering Multimodal Large Language Models Decoding for Context-Aware Safety
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of context-aware safety in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The authors argue that existing safety methods are often unbalanced: they can be oversensitive, refusing benign queries, or undersensitive, failing to detect visually grounded risks. The goal is to make MLLMs better at deciding when to refuse or answer based on both the user query and the accompanying image context.

To solve this, the paper proposes SafeCoDe, a lightweight, model-agnostic decoding framework with two stages. First, it uses contrastive decoding between a real image and a Gaussian-noised version of that image to surface tokens sensitive to visual context. Second, it applies a global-aware token modulation step, using an auxiliary MLLM judge to produce a safe/unsafe verdict that dynamically boosts or suppresses refusal-related tokens during decoding. The method is evaluated on several open-source MLLMs, including LLaVA-1.6-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, InstructBLIP-7B, and Idefics-9B-Instruct.

The study is not about teachers, K-12 classrooms, or educational deployment; it is a technical safety paper on multimodal AI systems. Across contextual safety benchmarks, SafeCoDe improves refusal behavior in both unsafe and benign contexts while preserving utility on general multimodal tasks. The authors conclude that combining visual contrastive signals with global safety verdicts can reduce both oversensitivity and undersensitivity, but they note a limitation that the approach currently assumes access to model logits, making it less directly applicable to fully black-box systems.

interventions.use_case: safety-aware contrastive decoding for multimodal large language models using visual contrastive signals and global verdict-guided token modulation to improve context-sensitive refusals

finding.finding_summary: The paper evaluates whether SafeCoDe improves context-aware safety behavior in multimodal large language models, which is a system-level governance/safety outcome rather than a learner outcome. Across four MLLM backbones, it reports consistently better balance between undersensitivity and oversensitivity, with substantially improved contextual safety scores and lower attack success rates on external safety benchmarks, while preserving utility.
finding.measure: Contextual safety accuracy/rejection rate on MSSBench and MOSSBench; attack success rate (ASR) on MM-SafetyBench, Hades, and FigStep; downstream utility on MMMU, MIA-Bench, MathVista, and MMVet
